summary: CHARTER: 'have a world class mermaid-editor like its viewer counterparts, while being performant and reliable' (disposition: feature) = raise the CODE-EDITING + render-pipeline loop to the polish of the app's already-mature VIEWER (pan/zoom, theming, sequence auto-coloring, multi-format export), benchmarked against mermaid.live, without regressing performance/reliability. USER OUTCOME: while typing Mermaid, the last valid diagram stays visible (dimmed) during a typo, the exact error line is flagged inside Monaco (red squiggly + full message), context-aware completions/snippets speed authoring, and there is no blank flicker, no DOM leak, and snappy re-renders. This round's job was to KILL the 6 blocking open questions that failed the prior two spec attempts; I resolved ALL of them with empirical + visual evidence at baseSha af47d8b (build present in dist/, node_modules installed, 127 unit tests pass baseline). KEY NEW FINDINGS: (Q5 OFFLINE — DECISIVE) Monaco is loaded FROM CDN at runtime, not bundled: @monaco-editor/loader's baked default is paths.vs='https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/monaco-editor@0.55.1/min/vs' (grep-verified in node_modules/@monaco-editor/loader/dist AND in dist/assets/CodeEditor-*.js), there is NO loader.config() call anywhere in src/, monaco-editor is NOT a direct dependency (only @monaco-editor/react is), and no monaco chunk exists in dist/assets. ARCHITECTURE_GUIDELINES.md §1.1 lines 18-22 EXPLICITLY allow this: 'Works offline (after initial load)', 'Never introduce API calls to remote services (except for external library CDNs)', 'All features must work without network connectivity after initial page load'. So Monaco-from-CDN is consistent with the documented posture; RECOMMENDATION: ACCEPT the existing online-first Monaco CDN dependency; do NOT bundle Monaco locally (would add ~2-5MB + worker config, violating the 'don't add heavy deps / preserve lazy-load / bundle already ~1MB' perf constraint). Autocomplete/markers work the moment Monaco is loaded — the same prerequisite the editor already has — so 'always-on completion' is satisfied to the same degree the editor itself is. (Q4 CONFIG SANDBOXING — DECISIVE) Mermaid v11.12.2 needs NO custom sandbox: initialize() routes through setSiteConfig() which does `siteConfig = assignWithDepth({}, defaultConfig); siteConfig = assignWithDepth(siteConfig, conf)` (chunk-ABZYJK2D.mjs:2511-2513) — i.e. it RESETS to defaultConfig THEN merges on every call, so config does NOT accumulate. I empirically proved it: init#1 sets themeVariables.primaryColor='#abcdef'; init#2 (omitting it) yields primaryColor='#fff4dd' (base default) NOT the prior value; a nonexistent theme does NOT throw (falls back via themes_default.default.getThemeVariables, initialize() lines 1095-1101); and a good config after a bad one recovers (parse ok). CONCLUSION: a semantically invalid config cannot corrupt a subsequent valid render as long as each trusted render re-initializes with the intended full config (the app already does). If adopting the 'initialize only when normalized config changes' optimization, on a config-only failure simply do NOT advance the committed/last-good config and re-init with the last-good config — rollback is native. (Q2/Q3 MARKER PRECISION — DECISIVE) I measured parse-error shapes across families: JISON diagrams (flowchart, sequence, state, er, sankey) throw err.hash.loc.{first_line,first_column,last_column} AND message 'Parse error on line N:'; 'block' throws 'Lexical error on line N.' with hash={line:N-1} (no loc); LANGIUM/chevrotain diagrams (packet, architecture, pie) throw 'Parsing failed: unexpected character: ->X<- at offset: N, skipped K characters.' with NO hash/line but a char OFFSET; CRLF is handled correctly (line 3 error → loc.first_line=3). CRITICAL EDGE: Mermaid reports lines RELATIVE TO PREPROCESSED SOURCE (YAML frontmatter + %%{init}%% directives stripped): with 4 lines of frontmatter an error at EDITOR line 6 reported loc.first_line=2 (off by 4); a 1-line directive shifted by 1. So exact universal line-accuracy is INFEASIBLE with a naive mapping; the right standard is BEST-EFFORT BOUNDED PLACEMENT with the FULL MESSAGE ALWAYS VISIBLE (matches AC-14). Extraction order: (1) hash.loc.first_line/column (jison, precise), (2) regex /(?:Parse|Lexical|Syntax) error on line (\d+)/i on message, (3) hash.line+1, (4) /offset:?\s*(\d+)/i → convert char offset to line/col by walking the raw code, (5) FALLBACK when nothing extractable → RECOMMEND mark line 1 (whole-line) AND always surface the complete message in the error affordance + marker hover (keeps the in-editor error signal present; omitting the marker is also defensible but loses that signal). Optional enhancement: add frontmatter/directive line offset back for precise markers. (Q6 INVENTORY — DECISIVE) The canonical completion + starter-snippet inventory is the 20 DiagramType categories in src/types/index.ts, EACH already backed by a working, renderable example in DIAGRAM_EXAMPLES (21 examples; flowchart ×2) — and tests/e2e/diagrams.spec.ts already renders+asserts every one of the 20 (incl. C4 and all beta variants: sankey-beta, xychart-beta, block-beta, packet-beta, architecture-beta, kanban), so AC-18 ('every type has a snippet that renders') is pre-validated. The keyword/shape/arrow vocabulary for context-aware completion already exists verbatim in CodeEditor.mermaidLanguageDefinition (diagramTypes[26 declarations], blockKeywords, sequenceKeywords, classKeywords, ganttKeywords, gitKeywords, erKeywords, stateKeywords, c4Keywords, requirementKeywords, architectureKeywords). RECOMMENDATION: freeze the inventory to the 20 DiagramType categories (reuse DIAGRAM_EXAMPLES as snippets, mermaidLanguageDefinition as keywords); context-aware by first-non-comment line; generic keyword fallback for anything unrecognized. (Q1 EXPORT-ON-ERROR — DECISIVE via competitor) I drove BOTH apps headless and screenshotted: OUR app on error blanks the whole preview (measured svg count 1→0), shows a big centered 'Syntax Error' card, leaks 1 orphan node into <body>, and shows NO Monaco marker; mermaid.live on the SAME bad input KEEPS the last-good diagram visible-but-DIMMED, shows a red .squiggly-error on line 2 (count=1), NO blocking card, and leaves actions/export ENABLED. So the competitor precedent is: retain last-good SVG (dimmed) and KEEP image exports enabled. RECOMMENDATION for Q1: keep SVG/PNG/copy-image ENABLED against the last-good SVG with a low-emphasis warning (a toast like 'Exported last valid diagram — current source has errors' and/or the dimming cue), because it matches mermaid.live, preserves the existing currentSvgString-driven export contract (it will simply hold last-good instead of ''), and is more useful; copy-code/share/markdown always use the RAW current source (AC-07). RELIABILITY defects re-confirmed in the live build and source: (a) DOM leak — DiagramPreview calls mermaid.render(`mermaid-${Date.now()}`, code) with NO container (src/components/DiagramPreview.tsx:34-35) → I measured 1 orphan node in <body> after one failed render; fix = pass an offscreen container as render's 3rd arg + finally-cleanup; (b) redundant re-init — renderMermaid guard `if (!isInitialized || config)` (src/lib/mermaid.ts:156) is always truthy because DiagramPreview always passes config → initialize every keystroke; (c) out-of-order race — DiagramPreview awaits renders with no epoch/AbortController (needs a monotonic render token, AC-08); (d) production console.log at src/lib/mermaid.ts:83. TESTING: unit env mocks mermaid (src/test/setup.ts) and Monaco can't run in jsdom, AND node/jsdom even fails to load some parsers ('DOMPurify.addHook is not a function' for class/mindmap) — so Monaco markers/squiggly/completion + real error lines MUST be proven by Playwright e2e at :5000; unit tests cover pure logic (extractErrorLocation across the jison/langium/offset/frontmatter cases, last-good retention via mocked resolve-then-reject, container cleanup). The existing DiagramPreview error test only asserts '.diagram-preview-bg' exists (test file lines 60-75) so last-good retention will NOT break it. Sequencing: (a) reliability fixes → (b) retain last-good SVG + non-destructive affordance → (c) Monaco markers from the render error via onError→App→CodeEditor → (d) context-aware autocomplete/snippets → (e) DEFER viewer polish. A new docs/ADR/002-render-pipeline-error-resilience.md + ARCHITECTURE_GUIDELINES §2.1/AGENT.md update are expected since the DiagramPreview error contract changes.
